entry.title: News Summary: November 25, 2026
entry.summary:
Frontier safety dominated the cycle. Axios reports dozens of insiders at OpenAI and Anthropic believe unreleased models have outgrown internal safety controls. Anthropic countered with honeypot evaluations testing rogue-agent resistance, while a new benchmark showed frontier agents still fail everyday tasks.

  • OpenAI says GPT-6 models can design proteins with lab-validated binding activity — a major AI-for-science milestone; separately, an Anthropic researcher walked back parts of the AI-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof rollout
  • AWS launched the Bedrock Trusted Access API with enterprise safeguards and data controls for Claude deployments
  • AI financing jitters spread: Anthropic shares fell below IPO price after a $1.3 trillion debut, and the tech sell-off resumed as Jensen Huang's Nvidia return euphoria faded

entry.title: News Summary: November 24, 2026
entry.summary:
OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra delivered the standout frontier milestone: the first machine-verifiable Lean proof of Smoktunowicz's gap theorem using an original proof strategy no other AI had found. Anthropic launched Claude Ship, pushing agents into autonomous code review, fixes, and approvals.

  • OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki disclosed internal perplexity scores for the GPT series and urged rivals to adopt shared safety limits before systems outpace oversight
  • Virginia and Oregon filed the first state lawsuits against SpaceX/xAI over Grok-generated CSAM and nonconsensual imagery — a landmark AI enforcement action
  • Amazon acquired Decart for $7.5B ahead of Trainium commercialization; Sierra raised $1.75B at a $30B valuation
  • xAI shifted to renting compute — reportedly $3.1B/month to Anthropic and $800M to Google — inverting AI industry economics

entry.title: News Summary: November 23, 2026
entry.summary:
OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol (GA 2026-11-17) drew early evaluations: answers are shorter and more direct, but transparency lags Anthropic's Claude. A rigorous new benchmark found AI coding agents—even frontier models—complete fewer than 1 in 10 tasks in simulated workplace conditions, challenging the autonomous-agent narrative.

  • Agentic reality check: Major US banks are banning third-party AI agents from customer accounts and shifting liability to users. Perplexity launched a Monitor API for scheduled web surveillance. Google previewed Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API for large tool libraries.
  • Safety and governance: OpenAI's chief scientist outlined measuring development speed as a precursor to limits. The Red Cross warned time is running out to regulate autonomous weapons.
  • Security and infrastructure: Researchers exposed cheap inference providers stealing API keys and snooping on requests, prompting OpenRouter remediation. Columbia/CertiK's TensorLean formally verifies GPU kernels and surfaced real bugs.
  • AI and mathematics: Ken Ono gave a firsthand account of Claude-assisted work proving the Riemann hypothesis, corroborating a verified landmark result.

Note: four items were excluded as duplicates of earlier coverage, including verification follow-ups on the Riemann proof and secondary coverage of NVIDIA's Alpamayo 2 Edge.

entry.title: News Summary: November 22, 2026
entry.summary:
UN talks on autonomous weapons collapsed in Geneva after Russian objections, leaving AI warfare ungoverned.

Frontier and product releases:

  • Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight 26.4B-parameter looped MoE that runs on a 32GB Mac
  • Baseten launched Bison-1 and Groundhog-1, open-weight decision models built on Gemma 4
  • Signal began blocking mobile screenshots, framing AI surveillance as an existential threat to private communication
  • Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq under ticker ANT at $83/share in a record IPO amid a broader AI-led market correction
  • Nvidia researchers argued giant context windows are a dead end; CoreWeave's debt-fueled datacenter buildout drew bubble comparisons

entry.title: News Summary: November 21, 2026
entry.summary:
Security and privacy dominated lab news:

  • OpenAI detailed its layered anti-distillation stack and cut reasoning-extraction success rates on GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol
  • Research embedding 2 million canary tripwires exposed systemic privacy failures in AI gateways like OpenRouter and Vercel
  • Signal began blocking screenshots on iOS 27 and Android to stop OS-level agents (Gemini, Siri AI, Muse) from reading private chats

In frontier research, unverified claims of an AI-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof via Claude — alongside a rival human proof — await scrutiny. NVIDIA open-sourced Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, a continuous diffusion LM family, and Bloomberg found China's AI-exposed job postings declining 10pp faster than other roles. Google launched an AI-first search homepage and brought computer-use agents to Gemini on Mac.

entry.title: News Summary: November 20, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic's record-breaking Nasdaq debut dominated coverage. Dario Amodei used the opening bell to recommit to pacing AI development, while analysts flagged circular-financing risk tied to compute commitments with Amazon and Google.

  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid a scandal — a seismic leadership shock at AI's core compute supplier
  • Tightened US export controls cut Chinese labs off from chips and overseas cloud; Moonshot AI abandoned a $150M Indonesian deal
  • Microsoft's buyout offer to 60,000 employees signals AI-driven organizational change
  • Google built a synthetic "mirror dimension" internet to test Chrome agents and rolled out Gemini computer-use on macOS
  • IEA projects datacentre carbon emissions up 70% by 2030 as the AI buildout leans on fossil fuels

The day paired a historic capital-markets moment with real frontier-model progress, marking a shift toward public-market scrutiny of lab safety commitments and agentic-AI infrastructure.

entry.title: News Summary: November 19, 2026
entry.summary:
The week's frontier narrative centered on Nvidia's upheaval and Microsoft's agent-first pivot. Nvidia stopped selling Hopper H200 chips to China, while interim CEO Colette Kress led the first all-hands since Jensen Huang's ouster. Washington plans further chip export restrictions, reportedly tied to the Huang scandal, clouding the Trump China trip.

  • Google DeepMind shipped Gemini 4 Neon, its newest frontier multimodal model, extending a rapid Gemini 4 release cadence (following Hydrogen, Carbon, Argon)
  • OpenAI confirmed frontier models (GPT-6 Astra) are optimizing production silicon, and opened unreleased models to four independent auditors including Apollo Research and METR — a governance first
  • Microsoft Ignite: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint now run inside Copilot in an agent-first inversion of Office; Nadella predicted agents will reshuffle web economics
  • Wired exposed Artex, a point-and-shoot AI hacking tool democratizing cyberattacks; Citi joined banks disclaiming liability for customer AI agents

entry.summary:
